description.text: Atmos Energy Corporation, a natural gas-only distributor, is an S&P 500 company headquartered in Dallas and incorporated in Texas and Virginia. We safely deliver reliable, efficient, and abundant natural gas through regulated sales and transportation arrangements to approximately 3.4 million residential, commercial, public authority, and industrial customers in eight states located primarily in the South. We also operate one of the largest intrastate pipelines in Texas based on miles of pipe. Atmos Energy's vision is to be the safest provider of natural gas services. We will be recognized for exceptional customer service, for being a great employer, and for achieving superior financial results. Our operating strategy is focused on modernizing our business and infrastructure while reducing regulatory lag. This operating strategy supports continued investment in safety, innovation, environmental sustainability, and our communities.

about.description_short: Atmos Energy Corporation, a natural gas-only distributor, is an S&P 500 company headquartered in Dallas. We safely deliver reliable, efficient, and abundant natural gas to approximately 3.4 million distribution customers in over 1,400 communities across eight states located primarily in the South. As part of our vision to be the safest provider of natural gas services, we are modernizing our business and infrastructure while continuing to invest in safety, innovation, environmental sustainability, and our communities. Atmos Energy manages proprietary pipeline and storage assets, including one of the largest intrastate natural gas pipeline systems in Texas.

analysis_md:
# ATO — Atmos Energy Corporation
v5 run, 2026-10-14. In scope (market cap $26.324B at $163.94, nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Guidance and quarter figures are from cited search results, as noted.

## What it is
Dallas-based regulated natural gas utility: the largest pure-play gas distribution company in the US footprint model — local distribution across eight states (Texas-heavy) plus Atmos Pipeline–Texas (APT), an intrastate transmission/storage system riding Permian/Waha flows. Essentially all earnings are regulated. The model is rate-base compounding: a ~$26B capital plan for fiscal 2026–2030 (over 85% safety/reliability), rate base guided from $18.8B in FY2025 to $40–44B by FY2030, and EPS growth guided at 6–8% through fiscal 2030 (search results). Fiscal year ends September 30.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $4,702,755,000; net income $1,198,754,000; operating cash flow $2,049,456,000; capex $3,561,399,000 (tag: PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets); SBC $12,731,000 (tag: ShareBasedCompensation); D&A $734,745,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$1,524,674,000 = −$9.50/share** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_total_latest_fy −$1,524,674,000, base_oe_latest_per_share −$9.4952). Capex exceeds operating cash flow by a wide margin — structural for a utility in a heavy pipeline-replacement / rate-base build cycle, not a one-off year.
- **OE positive only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years** (dcf_numbers.json): FY2021 −$3,065,046,000 / FY2022 −$1,477,579,000 / FY2023 +$643,592,000 / FY2024 −$1,214,087,000 / FY2025 −$1,524,674,000 (financials_history.csv, oe_conservative). The single positive year, FY2023, is the Uri-recovery artifact discussed under NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE below, not a run-rate.
- Maintenance version FY2025: $1,330,460,000 (financials_history.csv, oe_maintenance) — positive, and that gap between the two definitions is the story: most utility capex is growth/safety capex that enters rate base and earns an allowed return, so the conservative definition (OCF − total capex − SBC) is the harsher yardstick, and it is the sweep's base case.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): −$7.95/share** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_normalized_per_share −$7.9526, source median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; latest FY alone is −$9.50/share). Both are negative, so the choice of base does not change the verdict. No TTM pin was applied — see STALE_FY below.
- Balance sheet: the engine's net_debt_latest is null (the long-term-debt tag is absent from the recent companyfacts periods in financials_history.csv), so no net-debt figure is stated here rather than hand-computed. Shares diluted (latest): 160,573,000, with the share count growing at a 5.15%/yr CAGR (dcf_numbers.json share_cagr) — recurring equity issuance funds a large share of the capital plan and dilutes per-share compounding.

## Moat: 6/10 — durable regulated monopoly, capped economics
Justification: Exclusive regulated gas-distribution franchises with captive, essential-service customers and rider mechanisms that put new capex into rates quickly, plus the APT intrastate pipeline/storage franchise in Texas — a durable, visible rate-base compounding machine ($26B FY2026–30 plan, rate base guided $18.8B → $40–44B). Capped at 6 because regulators set the allowed return (no pricing power beyond rate cases and riders), Texas political/regulatory scrutiny of riders and customer bills is rising, safety litigation is a live exposure, and the plan is funded with continuous debt plus equity issuance that grows the share count ~5.2%/yr, diluting the rate-base growth per share.
- FOR: Exclusive regulated gas distribution franchises — captive, essential-service customers across eight states, Texas-weighted; rider/rate mechanisms recover safety and reliability capex quickly (annualized operating-income increases of $396M implemented fiscal YTD 2026, $227M of rate increases — Q3 2026 call highlights, search results); $26B FY2026–2030 capital plan with rate base guided from $18.8B to $40–44B by FY2030; APT intrastate pipeline and storage benefits from Permian/Waha through-system demand (APT spreads averaged $4.66 vs $1.77 prior year, fiscal YTD 2026); steady customer growth — nearly 51,000 added in the 12 months to June 30, 2026, ~39,000 in Texas.
- AGAINST: Regulators cap returns — allowed ROE and rider recovery are set politically; Jefferies cut its price target on October 1, 2026 (search results) citing Texas elections, scrutiny of regulatory riders and customer bills as the biggest risk to the shares; safety litigation and reputational exposure (a wrongful-death suit after the Dallas Oak Cliff gas explosion, per search results); growth is debt- plus equity-funded — a $700M 6% senior-note offering in October 2026 (8-K, search results) and share count +5.15%/yr, so per-share compounding lags rate-base growth; long-run gas-distribution transition risk if electrification policy turns against residential gas.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years by the sweep formula — academic here, since there is no positive OE stream to fade.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-14)
The final engine pass was run with moat 6 and default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 (offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp, multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25), but **the engine emits no scenario table, IV, or IRR: the normalized base OE is −$7.95/share, so there is no positive owner's-earnings path to discount at any scenario weighting.** Tier by numbers: **F**.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | n/a | 0.75 | Texas rider pushback, adverse rate cases, safety costs | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bear | 25% | n/a | 0.90 | Capex stays far above OCF; equity issuance accelerates | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Base | 30% | n/a | 1.00 | $26B plan keeps capex > OCF through 2030; OE stays negative | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bull | 25% | n/a | 1.10 | Rate-base growth converts to distributable cash sooner than history suggests | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Super bull | 10% | n/a | 1.25 | Structural FCF inflection | n/a — negative base | n/a |

- **Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not computable (negative base). Tier by numbers: F.**
- Sanity check on growth inputs: the engine's blended growth is 10.76% (dcf_numbers.json components: rev CAGR 5y 10.76%, rev CAGR 3y 3.83%, latest rev YoY 12.91%, OE/share CAGR 2y n/a), with the full −5pp share-count adjustment already deducted for the +5.15%/yr dilution. That blend sits above management's guided 6–8% EPS growth through fiscal 2030 (search results) because the 5-yr revenue CAGR spans the Uri-era revenue spike, but growth is irrelevant to the verdict: it multiplies a negative base. No scenario start was set below a recent print to manufacture conservatism, and none could rescue a negative base anyway.
- Recent prints (search results, for the record): fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026, reported August 5, 2026) diluted EPS $1.43 vs $1.16 in the prior-year quarter, on revenue of $879.06M; fiscal YTD 2026 net income $1.2B, or $7.33 per diluted share; fiscal 2026 EPS guidance reaffirmed at $8.40–$8.50 (raised earlier from $8.15–$8.35); fiscal YTD capex $3.1B with ~$4.2B planned for fiscal 2026. The earnings engine is healthy — it is the capex load, not profitability, that zeroes out conservative OE.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 2025-09-30, 12 months ago): ttm.py was run and exited non-zero with the message: "ttm.py: cannot compute TTM for ATO (CIK 731802): sbc: no post-FY YTD fact (no 10-Q since the 2025-09-30 fiscal year end)". Per the sweep rules the engine's median base is therefore used, with the reason stated here. The quarterly evidence that does exist (search results above) shows fiscal 2026 capex running at ~$4.2B for the year — above FY2025's $3,561,399,000 — against guided EPS of $8.40–$8.50, so a TTM base would be negative as well; the verdict is F on every available base. Note also that FY2026 itself ended 2026-09-30 and its 10-K is not yet filed, so the filed history cannot yet include it.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 5.15%/yr): this is equity-issuance dilution, not SBC — SBC is trivial at $12,731,000 in FY2025 (financials_history.csv). The count rose from 145,166,000 (FY2023) to 152,666,000 (FY2024) to 160,573,000 (FY2025) as Atmos funds the capital plan with forward sale agreements / ATM issuance (~$937M of net proceeds available under existing forward sale agreements at June 30, 2026 — Q3 2026 call highlights, search results). The engine already deducted the maximum −5pp via the share-count growth adjustment; the verdict does not double-count it, but a holder should: rate base compounds at double digits while per-share figures compound at the guided 6–8%.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025): two different mechanics, both visible in financials_history.csv. In FY2023, OCF of $3,459,743,000 ran far above net income of $885,862,000 — the recovery side of the February 2021 Winter Storm Uri gas-cost cycle: FY2021 OCF was −$1,084,251,000 when Atmos paid extraordinary purchased-gas costs, and the subsequent rate recovery / surcharge collections of those deferred gas costs inflated later OCF, which is also why FY2023 is the only positive-OE year in the last five. In FY2025, OCF of $2,049,456,000 vs net income of $1,198,754,000 is mostly the normal utility relationship — D&A of $734,745,000 is a large non-cash charge added back in OCF — plus working-capital timing. Neither divergence distorts the base in Atmos's favor: the conservative OE series is built from OCF directly, and it is capex ($3,561,399,000 in FY2025), not the NI/OCF gap, that drives OE negative.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Utilities): accepted in full — the OE/capex DCF fits regulated utilities poorly, because growth and safety capex is rate-base investment earning a regulated return, not value destruction. Confidence is graded **low** and the tier is read as "not modelable on this screen," not as "bad business."

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is the model's known blind spot, flagged as such: Atmos is a profitable, dividend-paying regulated monopoly (dividend $1.00/quarter, $4.00 annualized, paid September 8, 2026 — search results) whose conservative owner's earnings are negative in 4 of the last 5 years because utility capex runs above operating cash flow every year of a $26B rate-base build. The dividend and the build are funded the utility way — rate recovery plus continuous debt and equity issuance — which an OE screen reads as negative distributable cash.
- On numbers a utility investor actually uses (from search results, not the engine): fiscal 2026 EPS guided $8.40–$8.50 at a $163.94 price, long-term EPS and dividend growth guided at 6–8% through fiscal 2030 on rate base roughly doubling to $40–44B. That is a bond-like high-single-digit total-return profile before any multiple change — nowhere near Andrew's 15% hurdle on any defensible reading, so the F here agrees with the hurdle conclusion even though the model's mechanism (negative OE) is a sector artifact. No method range spanning tiers is claimed: on the v5 method there is one result, F.
- Hurdle-clearing price: not computable from this model — with no positive OE base there is no IV@15% at any price, and stating one would require a different model (dividend / rate-base), which is out of scope for this sweep. No tier override: the numbers tier F is retained, with the mismatch documented, rather than inventing a tier the v5 method cannot support.
- Real risks for a holder (outside the model): Texas regulatory/political pushback on riders and customer bills into the election cycle, safety-litigation cost and recovery (Dallas Oak Cliff), refinancing and funding a $26B plan at current rates while issuing equity into a +5.15%/yr share-count trend, and a premium multiple for the sector (P/E ~19–22x in search results) that leaves no room for a regulatory disappointment.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier by numbers F — no positive normalized conservative owner's earnings; OE DCF not supportable)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector-model mismatch: the F is a model artifact for a regulated utility, though no alternative reading clears a 15% hurdle either)
- One-liner: Durable Texas-heavy regulated gas monopoly, moat 6/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in 4 of the last 5 years (capex exceeds OCF on a $26B rate-base build; normalized base −$7.95/share) — Tier F on this screen; guided 6–8% EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
